data.title: Array Technologies plunges as UBS downgrades, seeing less available cash for M&A
data.description:
Array Technologies (ARRY) sinks 7.2% in Friday's trading as UBS downgraded the solar tracking manufacturer to Neutral from Buy with a $5 price target, slashed from $10, as the bank expects the use of preferred dividend payments through 2030 to reduce available cash for completing acquisitions.

"The transition of preferred dividends from payment-in-kind to cash-pay changes the outlook for FCF deployment" by reducing "cash available for deleveraging and growth investment, particularly opportunistic M&A, while competitors broaden their platforms through consolidation," UBS analyst Jon Windham said in a note.

The analyst said he expects Array (ARRY) will generate sufficient free cash flow to service the preferred dividends and estimates $162M of cumulative cash payments through 2030, but the company may have less flexibility to expand its product offering and defend its competitive position, increasing the company's reliance on organic growth and execution to deliver upside.

Windham said he remains positive on the direction of the U.S. solar industry, particularly for companies with domestic manufacturing footprints such as Array (ARRY), but he views the stock as fairly valued at ~5x estimated FY 2027 EV/EBITDA.

data.title: Volkswagen slashes profit guidance as China, restructuring charges, BEV adoption weighs
SOS Limited stock tumbles after agreement to sell 19M shares for $3.4M
data.description:
SOS Limited (SOS) stock sank 14% in Friday midday trading after the blockchain service and crypto company agreed to sell a block of its class A shares discounted to the market price.

The company entered a securities purchase agreement with certain "non-U.S. persons" under which SOS will sell a total of 19M class A ordinary shares at a price of $0.18 per share for a total purchase price of $3.42M. That represents a 77% discount to SOS's closing price of $0.70 on Thursday.

Proceeds will be used for further development and construction of its data center business, working capital, and general corporate purposes, it said.

Separately, SOS (SOS) said it entered a non-binding cooperation memorandum with an Indonesian company for the potential development of a ~500-megawatt wholesale AI and cloud data center in Indonesia, the company said Friday.

The framework cooperation memorandum sets out preliminary principles for cooperation, land and power arrangements, a funding mechanism and a six-month due diligence period. It's subject to the negotiation and execution of definitive transaction documents, completion of due diligence, financing, and applicable regulatory approvals. 

The final investment structure, equity percentages, valuation, board arrangements, and exit mechanisms are to be determined in subsequent definitive documents.

If the project advances, the company's phase I construction is expected to have a capacity of approximately 50MW. SOS (SOS) expects that it would seek to fund the platform through an equity and project-finance structure, with senior debt expected to be arranged with institutional lenders.

The memo contemplates a 10-year coal-index-linked pricing formula intended to provide competitive, market-responsive electricity costs, SOS (SOS) said.

data.title: Bloom Energy shares pause after two-day 8% surge in week of positive news
data.description:
Bloom Energy (BE) slides 3.5% in Friday's trading after surging 8% in a two-day rally that followed its unveiling of a new fuel cell architecture that generates continuous 800V DC power natively, which the company forecast will cut 1 GW AI data center non-compute capital spending by $3.6B.

The company said its approach will reduce the electrical infrastructure required between generation and compute, lowering capital cost, energy losses, and dependence on constrained components such as transformers and switchgear, where lead times are already measured in years.

BMO Capital's Ameet Thakkar said in a note that Bloom's (BE) strategic partnership with Brookfield, where Oracle would provide or facilitate up to $25B in financing to deploy Bloom's solid oxide fuel cell powered generation solution, is in the process of raising $6.4B in project financing for data centers sponsored by Meta and others, which would indicate diversification beyond Oracle for the partnership.

The analyst also said the New Mexico Supreme Court lifted its August stay that had prevented hearings to advance air permit proceedings for Oracle's 2.45 GW Project Jupiter data center, which will be powered by Bloom's (BE) energy server stationary power product.

data.title: Stock market edges down as Treasury yields rebound
data.description:
The stock market slipped Friday as Treasury yields reversed Thursday's retreat, with the 10-year note climbing back to the key 5.0% mark.

The S&P 500 (SP500) -0.3%, the Dow (DJI) -0.5%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) -0.3%.

The stock market rebounded Thursday after Wednesday's selloff, which followed the Federal Reserve's first rate hike since 2023.

Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid said he supported the central bank's decision earlier this week to hike rates as inflation has outpaced the Fed's 2% goal for more than five years.

Elsewhere on the economic calendar, industrial production growth stalled in August, falling short of expectations, while August leading indicators slipped and missed the consensus.

The 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) rose seven basis points to 4.75%, the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) increased seven basis points to 5.0%, and the 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) advanced four basis points to 5.34%.

data.title: Over half of Apple users plan to upgrade to iPhone 18: survey
data.description:
Evercore ISI's latest iPhone survey indicates Apple (AAPL) should enjoy a stronger-than-normal upgrade cycle and benefit from higher average selling prices.

"We see not just room for units to do well, but critically, we think pricing could be >20% driven by a combination of ASP increases, higher-priced SKUs, and a shift up in memory configurations," said Evercore analyst Amit Daryanani in a Friday investor report.

"Pricing trends continued to grow, with our survey reflecting an aggregate ASP of $1,374, up nearly 28% and well above our long-term survey average," he said.

The survey found that 53% of the nearly 4,000 consumers taking part plan to buy an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max. This is up from the average of 51%. It also discovered that 32% of respondents intend to buy the Pro Max compared to 29% in last year's survey. Fourteen percent said they will purchase Apple's new product, the iPhone Duo, compared to 9% last year who said they would buy the new iPhone Air. 

"Our 2026 iPhone survey points to a solid upgrade environment, with 61% of respondents planning to purchase an iPhone. This is slightly higher than last year's survey of 59% and marks the second strongest response in our survey's history and well above our survey average of 45%," Daryanani said.

Beyond the iPhone, there was a slight increase in respondents planning to upgrade their Apple Watch and AirPods.

Evercore retained its Outperform rating on Apple and increased its price target to $380 from $365.

data.title: Market's '3 Ps are all peaking' as rotation takes hold - BofA
data.description:
Bank of America Securities is warning investors that the stock market's (SPY) (DIA) (QQQ) primary drivers—positioning, profits and policy—are peaking, signaling a structural market rotation is already underway.

Market positioning is "too bullish," BofA reiterated in its latest Flow Show note, with the Bull & Bear Indicator triggering a 9.5 sell signal again and fund-manager positioning hitting the 100th percentile. Moreover, a record net 33% of fund managers now report companies are overinvesting.

 

Concurrently, profit expectations are moderating into 2027 as "GDP boom hopes are over," while monetary policy has shifted away from a "run it hot" posture, requiring higher bond (TLT) (ZROZ) risk premiums to restore credibility.

The macro shift is actively driving sector rotation. Since the Nasdaq's (QQQ) peak on June 1st, rising Federal Reserve hike expectations have deflated early leaders, specifically AI (AIQ) (AIEQ) enablers like "blue-collar semis" (SMH) (SOXX) and independent power producers, the note said.

 

 

For investors, BofA outlined a specific playbook: while it is "not yet time for defensives," a pivot toward quality (QUAL), value (VFVA), and yield looks prudent. However, the firm cautions that current market winners—commodities, credit and China bonds—represent key vulnerabilities heading into the fourth quarter.
